Verbatim_Quote: The enlistment contract cannot be extended for more than 48 aggregate months.

Subject: Records and Documentation
Question: A Sailor is separating from the Navy after completing a 4-year enlistment. As the PS processing the separation, you must ensure the correct NSIPS/ESR documents are submitted to the OMPF. Per MILPERSMAN 1070-111, which document is printed and e-submitted to the OMPF at the time of separation?
Answer_A: NAVPERS 1070/622 Agreement to Recall or Extend Active Duty
Verbatim_Quote: The following is a list of NSIPS/ESR documents that shall be printed and e-submitted to the OMPF upon reenlistment or separation: (1) NAVPERS 1070/605 History of Assignments

Subject: Records and Documentation
Question: A command does not have access to NSIPS and must manually process a personnel transaction. Per MILPERSMAN 1070-111, what statement or stamp must be included on all manually created NAVPERS forms before they are submitted to the OMPF?
Answer_A: "CERTIFIED CORRECT" followed by the CO's signature and command stamp
Answer_B: "ENTERED AND VERIFIED IN ESR" followed by the rank or grade, title, date signed, and signature of the ESR verifying official
Answer_D: "MANUALLY PROCESSED" with a memo from the command legal officer confirming system unavailability
Verbatim_Quote: Each manually created document must contain the following statement or stamp: "ENTERED AND VERIFIED IN ESR" followed by the "rank or grade, title, date signed, and signature of the ESR verifying official."

Subject: Records and Documentation
Question: A member in your division just got married and reports to you for administrative guidance after updating their RED/DA application. Per MILPERSMAN 1070-270, what must the member do with the printed NAVPERS 1070/602 "DA" and supporting documents?
Answer_A: Submit them to their command's legal office for notarization before filing
Answer_B: Mail them directly to PERS-222 within 10 days of the marriage
Answer_C: Provide them to a DEERS/ID Card Lab office within 30 days of updating their RED/DA application
Answer_D: File them permanently in their OMPF via a NAVPERS 1070/613 Administrative Remarks entry
Verbatim_Quote: The Service member will print a copy of the NAVPERS 1070/602 "DA" from "RED/DA Inquire" link and provide the copy with supporting documents to a DEERS/Real-Time Automated Personnel Identification System office (ID Card Lab) within 30 days of updating their RED/DA application.

Subject: Records and Documentation
Question: A member discovers that their date of birth has been recorded incorrectly in their service record since initial enlistment. Per MILPERSMAN 1000-120, which of the following is listed as the MOST PREFERRED documentary evidence to support the request for correction?
Answer_A: A formal board of inquiry must be convened before any date of birth correction is authorized
Answer_B: Two affidavits from relatives, friends, or disinterested parties who knew the member from the time of birth
Answer_C: A letter from the member's commanding officer confirming the discrepancy in writing
Answer_D: A copy of the birth certificate, officially certified by competent civilian authority
Verbatim_Quote: (1) Most preferred:  A copy of the Birth Certificate provided it is officially certified by competent civilian authority.

Subject: NEC Management
Question: A member completed a factory training course that qualifies them for a new NEC. The NEC did not auto-populate in NSIPS. Per MILPERSMAN 1221-021, why was the NEC not auto-assigned, and what is the correct action?
Answer_A: NECs from factory training require a waiver from NAVPERSCOM (PERS-40) before they can be awarded; NAVPERS 1221/6 is only used for NEC removals
Answer_B: NECs from factory training are not automatically assigned through CeTARS — the command must submit NAVPERS 1221/6 Navy Enlisted Classification Change Request to BUPERS-328 to award the NEC
Answer_C: NECs from all training sources are auto-assigned via CeTARS within 30 days; if the NEC did not appear, the member must contact the NSIPS helpdesk to report a system error
Answer_D: The member submits a NAVPERS 1070/613 Administrative Remarks documenting the course completion; the NEC will then be auto-assigned at the next advancement selection board
Verbatim_Quote: NECs earned through on-the-job training, job qualification requirements, personnel qualification standards, factory training, and or non-Navy training are not automatically assigned. In these cases, recommendations for assignment of NECs should be forwarded to the Bureau of Naval Personnel (BUPERS) Community Management Support Branch (BUPERS-328) by submitting NAVPERS 1221/6 Navy Enlisted Classification Change Request.

Subject: Reserve Participation
Question: You are a PS reviewing a Reservist's IDT attendance record over the past 12 months. The member has accumulated a total of 9 unexcused absences. Based on BUPERSINST 1001.39F, Chapter 11, what is the administrative status of this member?
Answer_A: The member is automatically transferred to the IRR once unexcused absences exceed 6 in any fiscal year
Answer_B: The member is still satisfactory because authorized absences bring the total below the threshold
Answer_C: The member must be designated as an unsatisfactory participant because 9 or more IDT periods in a running 12-month period were declared unsatisfactory or unexcused
Answer_D: The member is placed on a 30-day warning period before being officially designated as unsatisfactory
Verbatim_Quote: Members will be designated as unsatisfactory participants when 9 or more IDT periods in a running 12-month period are declared unsatisfactory or are unexcused absences.

Subject: Reserve Participation
Question: A Reservist asks you what determines their specific training and retirement requirements under BUPERSINST 1001.39F, Chapter 11. You explain that each member is assigned to a category that governs those requirements. What is the correct name of this category system?
Verbatim_Quote: This chapter identifies Navy Reserve Training and Retirement Categories (TRC) and sets forth requirements for members participating in the Navy Reserve.

Subject: Reserve Participation
Question: Per BUPERSINST 1001.39F, Chapter 11, what does it mean when an IDT period is recorded as an Authorized Absence (AA), and what effect does an assigned AA have on the number of regular IDT periods the member may perform that fiscal year?
Answer_A: An AA is assigned only for medical emergencies and has no effect on the number of IDT periods that may be performed
Answer_B: An AA is assigned for any excused absence and increases the number of IDT periods that may be performed by one
Answer_C: An AA counts as an unexcused absence toward the 9-period unsatisfactory threshold
Answer_D: An AA is assigned when there is no requirement to make up the missed IDT period and meaningful training is not available; each assigned AA reduces by one the number of regular IDT periods that may be performed for the fiscal year
Verbatim_Quote: AAs are assigned when there is not a requirement to make up missed IDT periods and meaningful training is not available. Each assigned AA reduces by one the number of regular IDT periods that may be performed per fiscal year.

Subject: Reserve Participation
Question: After reviewing attendance rosters, you identify a Reservist who failed to show up for an IDT period without prior notification or a valid excuse. Under BUPERSINST 1001.39F, Chapter 11, who is responsible for monitoring member participation and making this determination?
Answer_A: The member themselves, who must self-report the absence to NAVPERSCOM within 30 days
Answer_B: The commanding officer of the reserve unit (NOSC)
Answer_C: NAVPERSCOM (PERS-912), after the member's command submits a written request for administrative action
Answer_D: The member's senior enlisted leader, who documents the absence on the unit muster sheet
Verbatim_Quote: Criteria for Satisfactory Participation. COs of each NOSC are responsible for monitoring the participation of their members.

Subject: Reserve Participation
Question: An enlisted Reservist in your command has been officially designated as an unsatisfactory participant, and the NOSC CO believes the circumstances that caused this have been resolved. Based on BUPERSINST 1001.39F, Chapter 11 and Figure 11-1, what administrative action may the CO take, and what can happen if the member accrues one more unexcused absence during it?
Answer_A: The CO may place the member on a 6-month probationary period, and one more unexcused absence during it may result in the drill assignment being cancelled
Answer_B: The member is transferred to the USNR-S2 (inactive status) pending a formal board of inquiry
Answer_C: The member forfeits all retirement points earned in the year they were designated unsatisfactory
Answer_D: The member is immediately separated from the Navy Reserve with no further opportunity to correct their record
Verbatim_Quote: Enlisted personnel may be placed on 6 months probation for unsatisfactory participation if the NOSC CO believes the circumstances that caused the Reservist to be an unsatisfactory participant have been resolved. 2. If during the 6-month probationary period the member accrues one unexcused absence or fails to meet any other participation requirement, the member's drill assignment may be cancelled.

Subject: Non-Regular (Reserve) Retirement
Question: A PS2 asks you how many qualifying years of service a Navy Reserve member must complete before they are eligible to receive non-regular service retired pay under BUPERSINST 1001.39F, Chapter 20. What is the correct answer?
Answer_C: 18 qualifying years, which may be reduced for certain combat service
Verbatim_Quote: Unless otherwise provided by law, a Navy Reserve member must have completed 20 years of qualifying service to be eligible for non-regular service retired pay.

Subject: Non-Regular (Reserve) Retirement
Question: A Reservist is concerned that a year in which they drilled irregularly may not count toward retirement. Under BUPERSINST 1001.39F, Chapter 20, what is the minimum retirement point standard that must be met for an anniversary year to be counted as a qualifying year toward non-regular service retirement?
Answer_A: At least 48 IDT periods with no unexcused absences during the anniversary year
Answer_B: At least 27 retirement points, including the 15 membership points awarded annually
Answer_C: At least 90 days of active duty service during the calendar year
Answer_D: At least 50 retirement points earned during the anniversary year
Verbatim_Quote: In an anniversary year in which fewer than 50 points are credited, the earned points are added to the cumulative retirement point total, but that anniversary year is not a qualifying year creditable for earning a non-regular retirement.

Subject: Non-Regular (Reserve) Retirement
Question: A Reservist who has completed 20 qualifying years of service transfers to the Retired Reserve. They ask you at what age they can normally begin drawing their non-regular service retired pay under BUPERSINST 1001.39F, Chapter 20. What is your answer?
Answer_A: Age 55, provided they have completed at least 25 qualifying years
Answer_B: Age 57, with a mandatory application submitted no later than 6 months before that date
Answer_D: Age 60, unless eligible to receive it at a date earlier than age 60
Verbatim_Quote: Normally, be at least 60 years of age or be eligible to receive non-regular retirement pay at a date earlier than age 60, per 10 U.S.C., section 12731;

Subject: Non-Regular (Reserve) Retirement
Question: A PS2 asks you to explain what a "Gray Area Retiree" is under BUPERSINST 1001.39F, Chapter 20. Which of the following best describes this category of member?
Answer_A: A member who is currently receiving retired pay while simultaneously serving on active duty in a different component
Answer_B: A member who retired from active duty with fewer than 20 qualifying years and receives a reduced retired pay amount
Answer_C: A member assigned to USNR-S2 who is awaiting final transfer processing to the Retired Reserve
Answer_D: A Navy Reserve member who has completed the required service for non-regular retired pay, received a Notice of Eligibility (NOE), and transferred to the Retired Reserve, but has not applied for retired pay benefits and has not yet reached eligibility to draw it
Verbatim_Quote: Navy Reserve personnel who have not reached eligibility to draw non-regular retired pay, have received a Notice of Eligibility (NOE), and have not applied for retired pay benefits but have transferred to a Retired Reserve status after completing the required service for non-regular retired pay benefits under 10 U.S.C., chapter 1223. These members are often referred to as Gray Area Retirees.

Subject: Non-Regular (Reserve) Retirement
Question: A Reservist in your unit believes they have recently completed their 20th qualifying year toward non-regular service retirement. Under BUPERSINST 1001.39F, Chapter 20, what official document confirms they have accumulated sufficient qualifying service to be eligible for non-regular service retired pay, and who issues it?
Answer_A: A NAVPERS 1070/613 Administrative Remarks entry, signed by their commanding officer
Answer_B: A NAVPERS 1810/1 Navy Reserve Retirement Point Capture Form, submitted by their unit
Answer_C: A Notice of Eligibility (NOE), issued by NAVPERSCOM (PERS-912)
Answer_D: A DD Form 214 reflecting their cumulative Reserve service and qualifying point totals
Verbatim_Quote: Per 10 U.S.C., section 12731, NAVPERSCOM (PERS-912) will issue a NOE for non-regular service retired pay to each Navy Reserve member not on extended AD who has met all of the following conditions to qualify for non-regular service retired pay:

Subject: Enlisted Distribution
Concentration: Military Couple and Single Parent Assignment
Question: You are counseling a military couple who both desire co-location at their next duty station. Per MILPERSMAN 1300-1000, what driving distance is used as a guideline when determining whether two duty stations constitute co-location?
Verbatim_Quote: While there is no established maximum distance between duty stations for co-location, 90 driving-miles should be used as a guide when considering co-location requests.

Subject: Enlisted Distribution
Concentration: Military Couple and Single Parent Assignment
Question: A married military couple is both assigned to the same ship. The wife has completed 65% of her Prescribed Sea Tour (PST) and the husband has completed 40%. Per MILPERSMAN 1300-1000, which member will normally be reassigned first?
Answer_A: The wife, because she has completed the larger percentage of her PST
Answer_B: Neither is reassigned until both complete their full PST
Answer_C: The husband, because he has completed the smaller percentage of his PST
Answer_D: Both members are transferred simultaneously to the nearest shore duty billet
Verbatim_Quote: In the case of a member on shipboard duty who marries another member assigned to the same ship or the same shipboard embarking command, the member who has completed the larger percentage of his or her PST will normally be reassigned as soon as possible

Subject: Enlisted Distribution
Concentration: Military Couple and Single Parent Assignment
Question: A Sailor in your command is a single parent who has just received sea duty orders and is concerned about how single parents are handled in the assignment system. Per MILPERSMAN 1300-1000, which statement best describes Navy policy on single parent assignments?
Answer_A: Single parents may decline any sea duty assignment without consequence
Answer_B: Single parents are assigned only to CONUS duty stations by policy
Answer_C: Single parents are automatically assigned to shore duty for their first two tours
Answer_D: Single parents are assigned using the same procedures as other Service members, since a preferential policy would be discriminatory toward other members
Verbatim_Quote: 7. Single Parents. Single parents are assigned using the same procedures as other Service members. a. Navy Personnel Command recognizes the unique situations that occur when single parents are assigned to some types of duty and duty locations; however, a preferential assignment policy regarding single parents would be discriminatory toward other members.

Subject: Enlisted Distribution
Question: A member received OCONUS orders and elected an unaccompanied tour. After reporting, the member's family arrives in tourist status and is subsequently granted command sponsorship. Per MILPERSMAN 1300-308, how is the member's tour length adjusted?
Answer_A: The tour is automatically shortened by 6 months
Answer_B: No adjustment is made — the unaccompanied election is final once orders are executed
Answer_C: The member must complete only the original unaccompanied tour length regardless of sponsorship
Answer_D: The tour is adjusted to the accompanied tour length, or an additional 1 year on board, whichever is longer
Verbatim_Quote: Service members who report on unaccompanied orders to an overseas area that allows accompanied tours, then are later joined by dependent(s) at the Service member's expense, will have their tour adjusted to the accompanied tour length or an additional 1 year on board, computed from the date command sponsorship is granted, whichever is longer.

Subject: Enlisted Distribution
Question: A billet at an overseas duty station is being considered for designation as a "key billet." Per MILPERSMAN 1300-308, what makes a billet a key billet?
Answer_A: The continued presence of the officer, warrant officer, or senior enlisted (E-8/E-9) member is determined absolutely essential to the mission, and the position requires the accompanied tour length
Answer_B: The billet must have a 12-month unaccompanied tour length only
Answer_C: The billet must be vacant for more than 90 days
Answer_D: The billet must be designated for an E-7 or above, and the duty station must be OCONUS
Verbatim_Quote: Key billets are reserved for only those positions in which the continued presence of an officer, warrant officer, or senior enlisted Service member (E-8 or E-9) is determined to be absolutely essential to the mission of the activity, unit, or the U.S. presence in that area. Assignment to key billets must require Service members to serve the accompanied tour length, even if the Service member declines to serve the tour accompanied.

Subject: Enlisted Distribution
Question: A member serving a 24-month overseas accompanied tour receives PCS orders with a departure date that falls 57 days before their scheduled tour completion date. Per MILPERSMAN 1300-308, what is the administrative determination regarding completion of the overseas tour?
Answer_A: The member is considered to have completed the full tour, since reassignment up to 60 days early still counts as tour completion
Answer_B: The member must request a waiver from PERS-4 since only a 30-day early departure is authorized
Answer_C: The tour is considered incomplete and must be documented as a curtailment
Answer_D: The member forfeits overseas tour credit for the final 57 days
Verbatim_Quote: Shortened Tour Length. Tours must meet Department of Defense (DoD) overseas tour lengths. Service members may be reassigned up to 60 days prior to completion of the full tour length and be considered as having completed the full tour.

Subject: Enlisted Distribution
Question: Per MILPERSMAN 1300-1205 (Expedited Transfers), what may a Service member who is the victim of an offense listed as eligible under this article request prior to their normal projected rotation date?
Answer_A: A temporary reassignment within or outside their unit, or a permanent change of duty station
Answer_B: A transfer that can only be initiated by the alleged offender's command
Answer_C: An immediate discharge in lieu of transfer
Answer_D: Only a temporary local reassignment — PCS transfers are not authorized under this article
Verbatim_Quote: Service members who are victims of certain offenses stipulated in reference (a) may request a temporary reassignment within or outside their unit or a permanent change of duty station prior to their normal projected rotation date per references (b) through (i).

Subject: Enlisted Distribution
Question: A member has just arrived at their OCONUS duty station. A review of their screening documentation reveals a discrepancy that was not identified during the screening process, but the overseas command intends to let the member and dependents remain overseas. Per MILPERSMAN 1300-306, what is this report called?
Answer_A: An Overseas Screening Deficiency Report/Request for Early Return (OSDR/ER)
Answer_B: An Early Return for Cause Request (ERFCR)
Answer_C: An Overseas Screening Deficiency Report (OSDR) only
Verbatim_Quote: Overseas Screening Deficiency Report (OSDR) only. Submitted when a member and/or dependent(s) arrive overseas with a discrepancy that occurred during the screening process or was not identified during the screening process. This report documents the screening deficiency but does not require an early return as the overseas command intends to allow the servicemember and dependents to remain overseas.

Subject: Enlisted Distribution
Question: Your command is experiencing a critical manning shortage in a supervisory rating. Per MILPERSMAN 1306-108, which of the following meets the criteria to warrant submission of an Enlisted Manning Inquiry Report (EMIR)?
Answer_A: Any vacancy lasting more than 30 days
Answer_B: A rating supervisory shortfall of less than 70 percent manned, or a gapped 1 of 1 authorized billet leading to readiness impact
Answer_C: Any single unplanned loss of personnel, regardless of readiness impact
Answer_D: A rating manned below 90 percent, regardless of billet type
Verbatim_Quote: To warrant submission of an EMIR, the personnel shortage must meet one of the following categories: (1) Rating Manning. Current onboard (COB) manning or projected onboard (POB) manning in the applicable rating or closed loop/transitory Navy enlisted classification (NEC) code meets the following criteria: (a) rating supervisory shortfall of less than 70 percent manned, or (b) gapped 1 of 1 authorized billets leading to readiness impact.

Subject: Enlisted Distribution
Question: A Sailor assigned to an overseas duty station has had multiple documented incidents of misconduct in the local community. The commanding officer is considering submitting an Early Return for Cause Request (ERFCR). Per MILPERSMAN 1306-114, when is ERFC an appropriate action?
Answer_A: At any time at the commanding officer's discretion, with no other requirement
Answer_C: Only when all other efforts, such as training, counseling, guidance, and treatment, have been exhausted, and not in lieu of disciplinary action or administrative discharge
Answer_D: As a routine substitute for administrative discharge processing
Verbatim_Quote: ERFC is one of the strongest administrative actions used and should only be requested when all other efforts (i.e., training, counseling, guidance, treatment, etc.) are exhausted. ERFC will not be used in lieu of disciplinary action or administrative discharge, nor is it an excuse to transfer a problem Sailor to another command.
